applicant_utility.summary: This is an outgoing mobility grant for Poland-affiliated medical, pharmaceutical and health-sciences researchers, not a degree scholarship, and it opens only in irregular editions - the last one closed in 2024 and NAWA currently states it has no information about future calls, so any plan is contingent on a new announcement. When a call does open, the application runs through the NAWA ICT system and hinges on documents you cannot produce alone: an invitation from the foreign host centre plus opinions from your promoter and host-centre supervisor, all on the call's templates. Budget per month, not per total: funding is capped at PLN 29,500 per month (up to PLN 32,000 under the 2024-edition formula) and the one-off PLN 20,000 material support applies only to doctoral students and researchers on the scientific track staying longer than three months.
applicant_utility.best_fit: PhD students in medical, pharmaceutical or health-science doctoral schools, and doctorate-holding clinicians or academic teachers in Polish hospitals and universities who can secure a host-centre invitation abroad.
application_readiness_checklist: Monitor the NAWA programme page and the ongoing-calls list, because editions are irregular and unannounced gaps of a year or more have occurred
Identify a foreign host centre and obtain its invitation on the call's Appendix 2 template before the call opens
Agree the promoter's opinion (Appendix 3) and the host-centre supervisor opinion (Appendix 5) with both referees in advance
Prepare the confirmation of doctoral-student status (Appendix 4) if you are a doctoral applicant
Choose your track (teaching, scientific or clinical) and keep the stay within 1-6 months; only plan beyond three months if you qualify for the one-off PLN 20,000 support
common_rejection_risks: Missing or non-template host invitation, promoter opinion or supervisor opinion - these third-party documents are the usual failure point
Proposing a host centre in Russia, which the programme excludes
Planning a stay outside the 1-6 month window
Expecting the one-off PLN 20,000 on a teaching or clinical track, or on a stay of three months or less
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published support is a monthly package (stipend, living and accommodation lump sum, travel lump sum); anything above the monthly cap and costs outside these categories must be self-funded.
document_audit: All attachments must follow the call's appendix templates - a free-form invitation or opinion risks rejection
The proposal application form goes through the NAWA ICT system, not by email
Check which language version of each appendix the current call requires; the 2024 announcement and templates were published in English with Polish originals
alerts: No call is open and NAWA states it has no information about future calls - the next edition cannot be scheduled

The English programme page still carries the 2024-edition text with a '31 January 2024' deadline that predates the 5 December 2024 announcement; verify dates against the Polish announcement of any new call
Funding figures differ between the English page (PLN 32,000 per month, fourth-edition formula) and the current Polish page (PLN 29,500 per month cap for highest-cost countries)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: When a call opens: complete the application in the NAWA ICT system, upload the templated host invitation, promoter opinion, supervisor opinion and doctoral-status confirmation, then await evaluation and a funding agreement before the stay.

official.deadline_note: Standing published rule: the competition is announced every year at the beginning of December and applications are due 1 March. The 2026/27 competition closed on 1 March 2026 and that edition was inaugurated on 23 September 2026; the next announcement, expected in December 2026, would set a 1 March 2027 deadline. No 2027/28 deadline is published yet.
official.application_cycle: Annual: announced each December, applications due 1 March, studies run two semesters (September-June); the 2026/27 edition is currently underway
official.status_note: The 2026/27 competition closed on 1 March 2026; the new scholarship year was inaugurated on 23 September 2026 at the University of Bielsko-Biala and the 26th edition graduated on 25 June 2026. The programme runs an annual cycle, so the next competition is expected to be announced in December 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The offer publishes free access to university classes at the affiliated Polish universities and support from an academic advisor.

official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship and permanent residence in one of the ten eligible countries (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Tajikistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan); Russian candidates' participation is suspended; Polish residence-card holders and people living, working or studying in Poland at application are ineligible
official.international_eligibility: The programme is exclusively for candidates from the listed Eastern European, South Caucasus and Central Asian countries; the scholarship brings them to Poland
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Studies limited to areas related to systemic and economic transformation listed in the announcement: economics and management, management in business/NGO/culture/education/healthcare, public administration, law, social sciences, political science and international relations, development policy and humanitarian aid, environmental protection, security issues, crisis management, and war-reconstruction-related fields (2026/27); aimed at civil servants, lawyers, entrepreneurs, NGO/culture/media/education managers, academic teachers and journalists
official.research_requirement: A project of stay of 4,000-6,000 characters outlining the planned paper must be submitted with the application; grantees write two term papers and defend a final project of at least 50 pages, normally in late May or the first half of June (English-track grantees write all papers in English)
official.duration: 9.5 months: preparation and orientation session plus two semesters at one of four academic centres (Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw, Lublin), a Polish language course (October-June), three integration conventions, compulsory volunteering, and a professional internship of at least two weeks
official.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program, founded in 2000 by the Polish-American Freedom Foundation and administered since 2016 by the Leaders of Change Foundation with some scholarships funded by NAWA since 2019, supports young leaders and experts from Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus and Central Asia with a nine-month non-degree study stay in Poland. Over nearly 25 years more than 1,000 alumni have completed the programme, which combines two semesters of university classes, a professional internship, volunteering and a final project, funded with a stipend, accommodation, insurance and travel support.

official.program_type: Non-degree professional development scholarship (two-semester study programme with internship)
official.english_requirement: Studies may be carried out either in Polish or English, with B2 required in the language of study; candidates studying in English must indicate a specific English-language offer at one of the four academic centres and need basic Polish at A1 level; candidates whose Polish is insufficient at the interview may take a language exam in mid-June, the result of which decides final qualification

applicant_utility.summary: This is a nine-month, fully covered non-degree study scholarship in Poland for graduates from ten eligible countries, so the real competition is over the written project and the interview rather than over funding. Applications follow a strict annual rhythm - announced each December, due 1 March - and the next window opens around December 2026 for the 2027/28 year, because the 2026/27 edition already started in September 2026. Money-wise the programme currently advertises a PLN 25,200 stipend in 9 monthly installments (the 2026/27 announcement said PLN 22,500) plus roughly PLN 4,500-5,000 a month in accommodation, insurance, transport and travel support, so living costs are largely handled. The two reference letters and the 4,000-6,000-character project statement are where applications are actually won or lost.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Professionals under 40 from the eligible countries with a completed degree, at least two years of work experience and a concrete transformation-related project they want to develop in Poland and take home.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the project statement (4,000-6,000 characters with spaces) early - the online form cannot be registered below 4,000 characters
Line up two referees who know your professional work (family members and partners are barred) and have their letters ready to send when the call opens
Choose a specific Polish- or English-medium study offer at one of the four centres (Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw, Lublin) and name it in the form
Prepare Polish to at least A1 (needed even for English-track study) and aim for B2 in your language of study
Confirm you are not living, working or studying in Poland and hold no Polish residence card before applying
common_rejection_risks: A project statement under 4,000 characters or too generic - the form refuses to register and field experts weight this section heavily
Reference letters from relatives or partners, or letters arriving after the deadline
Being based in Poland (work, study or residence) at the time of application
Missing the 1 March deadline while waiting for the December announcement to be re-posted or translated

Assuming your country can study in English - the state portal study.gov.pl still states English-medium study is not possible for candidates from Belarus and Ukraine, so confirm language options with the Programme Office before choosing a track
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the stipend and the roughly PLN 4,500-5,000 monthly package, grantees fund personal spending, any travel beyond the agreed return-ticket limit, and the parts of optional post-graduate studies and conferences that are only subsidized.
document_audit: The application form is completed online while the diploma copy and reference letters go by e-mail - a paper application by post is not accepted
No employment certificates are required, but the work history entered in the form is confirmed by the candidate's signature, so keep it exactly accurate
Reference letters must be in Polish, English or Russian and should use the reference-letter template published with the current call
alerts: The competition is strictly annual - announced in December, closing 1 March - so missing the window costs a full year
The stipend rises between editions (PLN 18,000 on the state portal, PLN 22,500 for 2026/27, PLN 25,200 in the standing offer), so budget from the current announcement rather than older listings
Russian candidates' participation has been suspended since February 2022 even though Russia appears in the general country list
study.gov.pl still shows outdated figures (PLN 18,000 and five academic centres including Poznan) - rely on kirkland.edu.pl
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Watch for the December announcement, complete and register the online form before 1 March, e-mail the two reference letters and diploma copy to the Programme Office, then pass formal screening, expert review (Stage 3 invitations by about 25 March) and the March/April interview.
